generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

traits.note: The Families of Flowering Plants of Australia's account of the family (with Watson and Dallwitz's DELTA), as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): sepals and petals (2-)4(-7), usually 4; a floral tube prolonged above the ovary except in Ludwigia (and in fireweed, whose petals are free at their base); stamens usually 8, (4-)8; ovary inferior, usually of 4 joined carpels.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 289 Onagraceae: herbs, rarely shrubs; leaves simple, opposite or alternate; stipules mostly absent or falling early; fruit a capsule, berry or nut.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Onagraceae with Trapaceae: flowers regular or irregular as coded, a state the authors qualify keeping its word (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py).

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Onagraceae with Trapaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 347, family Onagraceae: leaf arrangement spiral, opposite or whorled, usually; read as {"alternate": "often", "opposite": "often", "whorled": "often"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 347, family Onagraceae: inflorescence spike, panicle or solitary flowers, usually; read as {"panicle": "often", "solitary": "often", "spike": "often"}.
